name: Gesher Benot Ya‘aqov recurrent fire use
description: At an ancient lakeside site, clustered burned residues in repeated occupation horizons support researchers’ interpretation of recurrent hominin use of fire.

impact.note: One community at one site; repeated fire use was a real ability for them, but no later practice is known to descend from this group.

places.note: Present-day country or region reference; ancient political boundaries are not implied.

date.label: approximately 0.78–0.79 million years ago
date.basis: The article calls the site 0.78 Ma in its introduction and 790,000 years ago in its site description. The chart range reflects these approximate expressions, not the full length of occupation or a formal dating interval.

events.statement: At Gesher Benot Ya‘aqov, Alperson-Afil interpreted clusters of burnt flint in eight occupation horizons of Layer II-6 (levels 1–7, including 4b) as evidence of recurrent fire use. At Level 2, a later thermoluminescence study found stronger heating in sampled flint near the centre of the main cluster.
events.caveats: Hearths are inferred from the burnt material. The thermoluminescence study sampled one horizon. How the hominins obtained or ignited fire is unknown.

evidence.locator: Spatial Analysis and Fire at Gesher Benot Ya‘aqov
evidence.supports: The author reports spatial clustering and repeated layers and interprets them as hearths.
The eight Layer II-6 occupation horizons contain local concentrations of burnt flint microartifacts, interpreted as traces of recurring hearths.

evidence.locator: 2017 Layer II-6 Level 2 and Fig. 2, Results and Table 3; corrected Fig. 4 (2018, e0190804)
evidence.supports: The small Level 2 transect showed a trend of decreasing heating intensity with distance from the main burnt-flint cluster.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the cited evidence for this precisely scoped record; not a claim of global origin.

caveats: The reconstructed behavior and site chronology are under study; no global first, known fuel protocol, or direct cultural descent is inferred.

research.note: The approximate age expressions were checked in an earlier review. The Layer II-6 scope and Level 2 measurements draw on the cited excavation analyses.

links.statement: Did hominins sustain the Level 1 fires with wood gathered along the palaeo-Lake Hula shore?
links.scope: Gesher Benot Ya‘aqov, Layer II-6 Level 1, one of the eight fire horizons.
links.finding: Charcoal and unburnt wood share abundant ash and olive. Allué and colleagues infer local procurement of available deadwood or driftwood as fuel.
links.caveats: Charcoal and burnt flint distributions do not precisely coincide. The source analyses one horizon and has investigators in common with the earlier Gesher fire studies.

evidence.supports: Compares burnt and unburnt wood and maps the charcoal against the older Level 1 flint inventory.
Documents the earlier burnt-flint counts in the same horizon.
